input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: § 12.4 is the only non-solicitation provision in the Agreement and it fails the fallback on every material term: it binds Customer only (not mutual), covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs eighteen months from termination rather than 12 months from the end of the person's involvement, bars "engage" (an effective no-hire) as well as solicitation, and contains no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It also sits awkwardly with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment" and is free to hire persons responding to general recruitment. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the restriction on Customer with a single surgical replacement, offering the narrow mutual fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Replace the one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-engage restriction with a statement that Customer has no non-solicitation restriction.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the restriction in § 12.4: it bound only us, ran eighteen months, reached anyone Vendor employed at any time rather than personnel involved in the Services, barred engagement as well as solicitation, and had no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Our position is no non-solicit on Customer; we could alternatively accept a mutual clause limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: Customer is subject to no non-solicitation restriction under this Agreement.
